title: airbaltic postpones key meeting bondholders 2026 09 11
text:
VILNIUS, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Latvia's airBaltic ​has rescheduled a meeting of bondholders that had been due to ‌take place on Friday, the carrier said in an email to Reuters, as it works to shore up its finances.
"The bondholders' meeting has been postponed to allow bondholders additional time ​to review the draft resolution and submit their voting instructions in a ​timely manner," the airline said.
The virtual meeting is now set to ⁠take place on September 15 at 1200 GMT.
The carrier, which is majority ​owned by the Latvian state, has said it is seeking financing from bondholders as it races ​to avert the risk of default.
AirBaltic had asked bondholders to approve a plan on Friday to raise up to €257 million ($298 million) through new super-senior debt due in 2027.
The carrier is ​a test case for the wider airline market where weaker operators that struggle ​to pass on higher costs face the biggest pressure from soaring jet fuel prices caused ‌by ⁠the Iran war.
The new bonds would take priority for repayment from collateral — which includes eight aircraft and seven engines — while notes due in 2029 would fall to third priority, which analysts said could be behind a spike in yields this ​week.
Yield on airBaltic's €380 ​million notes due ⁠in 2029 fell sharply on Friday, following a rise on Wednesday when the bond prices dropped to record lows.
The yield ​has jumped more than twentyfold this year, reflecting higher perceived ​risk. The ⁠carrier first signalled major financial pressure in March after its jet fuel bill surged in the wake of the war in the Middle East.
Polus Capital, the credit ⁠fund committing ​to at least half of the new issue ​that will be voted on Tuesday, declined to comment.
($1 = 0.8613 euros)
